title: CitationEvalSet
description: Edge-case evaluation set for field-level citation generation. Each item names one JSON Pointer in a case's result.json, tags the edge cases it exercises, states the expected behaviour, and carries ground-truth evidence (anchors in citations/v1 shapes) split into acceptable / secondary / forbidden. Matching and scoring rules live in eval/README.md.

anchorSchema.description: Reference to the Anchor definition the ground-truth anchors conform to.

expectations.description: Human-readable definition of each `expect` value and its pass condition.

categories.description: Edge-case taxonomy. Every category used by an item must be declared here.

id.description: Unique within the set. Convention: `<case-number>.<pointer with / -> .>`.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer into the case's result.json.

value.description: The value at `pointer` in result.json, copied verbatim so the item is self-describing. The validator checks it still matches.

fieldType.description: `type` from result-definition.json for this field (string, int, float, boolean, array, enum, ...).

fieldDefinition.description: Truncated `description` from result-definition.json. Included because several expectations (defaults, N/A rules, exclusions) follow directly from it.

categories.description: Edge-case tags; each must be a key of the top-level `categories` map.

minAcceptableMatches.description: For `expect: cite`, how many distinct `acceptable` entries must be matched to pass (used for multi-citation items).

minRequiredContextMatches.description: When `requiredContext` is present, how many distinct context entries must be matched by produced anchors whose role is `context`.

acceptable.description: Ground-truth evidence. For `cite`: any-of (subject to minAcceptableMatches). For `context-only`/`empty`: tolerated context.

requiredContext.description: Context evidence required in addition to an acceptable value match. Its anchors must use role `context`; produced value/label anchors do not satisfy this requirement.

secondary.description: Evidence that is not wrong but not sufficient on its own (derived artifacts, over-wide boxes, partial support). Matching it is neither a pass nor a false positive.

forbidden.description: Known distractors. Matching any of these is a false positive regardless of `expect`.

label.description: Human-readable description of where this evidence is.

quote.description: Verbatim source text under the value-role anchors (before normalization to the result format).

anchors.description: One logical piece of evidence, possibly several anchors (label + value, or two spans). A produced citation matches this evidence if it matches a value-role anchor (or any anchor, when every anchor is label/context). When label or context anchors are present, the same citation must also cover one of them: the words around the value that identify the field.
